subject: CarePath model qualification & guardrail plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference>
To: Emily Jenkins <emily.jenkins@carepath.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-09-27T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: model fit shortlist + safety/guardrail approach

Hi Emily — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of needs (from call):
- Use-case: clinician-facing summarization & triage notes for telehealth visits (~2k tokens typical input).
- Sensitive categories: PHI, mental health crisis, self-harm ideation — must refuse or escalate.
- Throughput: ~150 requests/min during peak hours; latency SLO < 400ms 95th for short responses.
- Compliance: SOC2 + regionally segmented logging (US).

Initial model-fit recommendations:
- Candidate A: open-llm-giant-3b (quantized) — best cost/throughput for template summarization.
- Candidate B: redwood-guarded-7b — stronger refusal patterns on mental-health probes, slightly higher cost.
- Fallback: redwood-lite-1.4b for burst/low-cost routing.

Benchmarks & artifacts (attached and linked):
- carepath_model_benchmark.csv — coarse token/latency/cost across your sample prompt set.
- prompt_set_v1.yaml — the seed prompts we used for safety/refusal probes and summary templates.
- Drive folder with full logs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bCarePathBenchmarks

Safety and policy approach (high level):
- Refusal strategy: policy-based pre-check + model-level refusal testing. For suicide / harm / PHI we recommend a strict refusal template that returns a standardized escalation object and links to your escalation webhook (we can mock during eval).
- Prompt-based guardrails: explicit instruction + calibrated temperature and refusal tokens. We'll run structured A/B evals to measure false-positives on refusal.
- Regression detection: per-prompt quality probes, weekly snapshot tests; we'll wire alerts if generation quality drops >5% on your key prompts.

Proposed next steps: 
1) You share a 200–400 sample of real (redacted) visits for us to run the benchmark (we can sign an NDA / limited dataset).
2) We run a 5-day pilot: model scoring, refusal evaluation, and latency profiling (we'll provide the CSV + report).
3) Joint call to review results + lock on a dedicated capacity estimate and playbook for guardrails.

Can you do a redacted sample by EOD Friday (10/01)? Also, any internal compliance contacts we should loop in for SOC2 evidence mapping?

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference | (415) 555-0176
From: Emily Jenkins <emily.jenkins@carepath.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-09-28T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit shortlist + safety/guardrail approach

Thanks, Vivek — this is very helpful. A few clarifying questions before we hand over samples: 

1) Sample redaction — we can remove direct identifiers but will keep clinical context. Is that acceptable for the benchmark?
2) The "refusal template" you mention — can you share a short example of the JSON escalation object you'd return so our engineers can wire it to the triage webhook?
3) For the SOC2 mapping: who at Redwood should our security lead contact? We will need to align on log retention policies and evidence you can provide for a vendor assessment.

Tentative: we can prepare a first batch of 250 redacted visits by Friday but need the escalation example and a short checklist for redaction.

—Emily
Emily Jenkins
Head of Product, CarePath Health
emily.jenkins@carepath.ai | (617) 555-4490
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference>
To: Emily Jenkins <emily.jenkins@carepath.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-09-29T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit shortlist + safety/guardrail approach

Emily — great questions. Answers inline: 

1) Sample redaction: yes — removing direct identifiers (names, MRNs) while preserving clinical context is exactly what we need. Please do include some edge cases (short ambiguous notes, references to self-harm) so we can test refusal behavior. Attached is a short redaction checklist (SOC2_evidence_request.pdf includes items we typically request).

2) Escalation object example (previewed below) — we'll include the canonical JSON in the Drive folder but here's a simple example: 
{
  "escalation": true,
  "reason": "refusal_policy: self_harm_indicator",
  "confidence": 0.92,
  "action": "webhook://triage.carepath/alerts",
  "metadata": {"prompt_id": "suicide_probe_v1"}
}

Note: we return the standard object and an HTTP 202 after a short backoff; your webhook can decide next steps. We'll also include a safe human-readable message fallback in the response body.

3) SOC2 mapping: loop in our Security Lead — Laura Bennett (laura.bennett@redwood.inference). She'll coordinate evidence (audit logs, retention policy, encryption at rest keys) and can do a quick sync next week.

Attachments included: carepath_model_benchmark.csv (initial run on your sample prompts), prompt_set_v1.yaml (seed prompts + refusal probes), SOC2_evidence_request.pdf (redaction checklist + evidence items).

Proposed: I blocked a 30-minute review slot for next Tue 10/05 at 10:00am PT to walk through the benchmark and escalation flow; Ben, would you join to cover pricing/ Dedicated capacity estimates?

Thanks — Vivek
